text:
Short answer: on bandwidth alone, yes — but the FMECA question cannot be closed with what has been supplied, so it is "not yet". All figures below are DEMO placeholders from the supplied demo note, not real project values.

What the material shows
- SWS has no fibre of its own; each unit reaches its base station over RS-485 duplex on CAT cable. The fibre is the control-system backbone between base stations and winches and carries the PLC's PROFINET traffic. The proposal is for the side A base stations to forward SWS logger data over that same fibre, next to PROFINET.
- Load check (DEMO): 10 hoists on side A x 2 SWS units per hoist x 100 kbps per unit = 2.0 Mbps of logger traffic on a 1000 Mbps fibre link, i.e. a fraction of 0.002 (0.2 %). Bandwidth is not the constraint.

Why the FMECA is not cleared
- No FMECA document of any revision is in the material, so there is no baseline severity/occurrence/detection or RPN for "loss of side A PROFINET fibre" to compare against. Also missing: PROFINET cycle time and device count, fibre core allocation and spare cores, optical link budget inputs, and the switch-port configuration for the logger traffic (marked [OPEN] in the note). "SWS" is not defined in any supplied glossary; the acronym is used here as written.
- The register has two open red items that the sharing proposal directly triggers. Both need a stated mitigation before sharing can be accepted.

Mitigations for the open red items
- DEMO-NET-001 (broadcast storm from an SWS port): put every base-station port that carries SWS logger traffic in its own non-PLC VLAN with storm control / broadcast rate limiting and a conservative ingress rate limit on each port; disable unused ports; keep the SWS side as RS-485 to the base station (as now) so no SWS unit is itself an Ethernet endpoint on the backbone. Verify with a storm injection test on a bench before site. Defer the PoE-for-SWS option (marked [OPEN], pending Ex) until it has been resolved, since it would change the port design.
- DEMO-NET-002 (SWS traffic reaches the PLC VLAN): segregate logger traffic from PROFINET by VLAN with no routing between them; forward logger data only to the logger via a dedicated port; apply QoS so PROFINET real-time frames keep priority on the shared trunk; configure PROFINET device ports untagged on the PLC VLAN only. Verify with a packet capture on the PLC VLAN showing zero SWS frames, and confirm PROFINET cycle-time margin once the cycle time and device count are supplied. If the fibre schedule shows spare cores, the stronger option is physical separation: run the logger traffic on a separate core pair so the PROFINET path is untouched.

What is needed to close the question
Approved FMECA revision with the baseline ratings for the side A fibre, PROFINET cycle time and device count, the fibre core schedule, optical link-budget inputs, the finalised switch-port configuration, and a glossary definition of SWS. Until these are supplied and the two red items are re-rated, the answer remains: bandwidth is fine (DEMO), FMECA not yet cleared.

The draft relies on QoS to keep PROFINET priority but never asks which PROFINET RT class is in use. If side A is IRT (class 3), sharing the medium with non-PROFINET traffic is not permitted on standard switches regardless of VLAN/QoS; if RT class 1, the trunk must preserve 802.1Q priority tags end …

The bandwidth figure assumes a 1000 Mbps fibre link. The link rate is not in the supplied material; if the side A backbone is 100 Mbps (common for PROFINET) the fraction is ten times higher, still small, but the draft should state the rate as an assumption rather than a given.

Verification of DEMO-NET-002 by 'a packet capture on the PLC VLAN showing zero SWS frames' is a snapshot and cannot demonstrate absence. A positive test (inject tagged/untagged test frames on the logger port and confirm they do not appear on the PLC VLAN) is the appropriate evidence, together with …

The draft does not say whether SWS logging has any safety or compliance role. If it does, the consequence of losing the logger path when the fibre fails (common-mode) needs to be assessed in the FMECA, not just the consequence for PROFINET.

The draft states the two red items are 'directly triggered' by the proposal and then gives mitigations, but it does not say who re-rates them or that the mitigations themselves must be entered as design requirements before re-rating; without that the 'not yet' conclusion has no closure path.
The disclaimer that all figures are DEMO placeholders is correct and should be kept; the conclusion 'bandwidth is fine' should carry the same caveat in the short answer, not only in the body.

text: The provisional 'not yet cleared' conclusion is appropriate, but bandwidth sufficiency and separation benefits need qualification.

findings.text: The 0.2% calculation establishes nominal incremental load only. It does not establish available bandwidth or PROFINET timing margin without existing utilisation, peak logger traffic, switch behaviour and cycle-time requirements. Qualify 'bandwidth is fine' accordingly.

Separate core pairs still share the fibre cable and potentially switches, power and routing. Clarify that VLANs and spare cores do not eliminate these common-cause failures, which must be assessed against the approved FMECA.
The cited note and tool output are not included in the review input, so the claimed topology, open register items and source-derived figures could not be independently verified.
